floating-action-button.name: Floating Action Button
floating-action-button.purpose: Expose one high-prominence contextual action above a surface without becoming a speed dial, quick action cluster, or navigation shortcut.

anatomy.rule: Circular or extended action target above the current surface.
Clarifies extended actions without replacing aria-label.
Separates the action from underlying content.
Shows keyboard focus, loading, pressed, and disabled states.

variants.description: Icon plus label when action clarity matters.
Compact action for dense or secondary surfaces.

floating-action-button.statePrecedence: disabled > loading > pressed > focus > hover > default

Energy.decision: Use semantic action, surface, and state color.
Energy.behavior: The component communicates action and priority without raw colors.

Voice.decision: Use concise labels and short contextual copy.
Voice.behavior: Text explains the local decision without pattern instructions.

Frame.decision: Use stable geometry, spacing, and target size.

Depth.decision: Use elevation only when the component floats above a surface.
Depth.behavior: Layering clarifies context without persistent workspace behavior.

Momentum.decision: Use Design System motion for state and layer transitions.
Momentum.behavior: Changes feel responsive and respect reduced motion.

State.decision: Use explicit state precedence from the contract.
State.example: disabled > loading > pressed > focus > hover > default

Tone.decision: Use warning or critical tone only with visible reason.
Tone.behavior: Risk is explained through copy and state.

Growth.decision: Escalate orchestration beyond one local control to patterns.

Symbol.decision: Use symbols as support for visible labels or accessible names.
Symbol.behavior: Icons accelerate recognition without replacing meaning.

Iconography.decision: Use Design System icon sizing and optical alignment.
Iconography.behavior: Symbols align with text and target size.

Accessibility.decision: Expose label, state, focus, keyboard, and dismissal or selection behavior.
Accessibility.behavior: Assistive technology can operate the component.

props.name: loading
props.notes: Shows busy state for the invoked action.

props.name: extended
props.notes: Shows the label beside the icon.

do: Use for one contextual primary action.
Keep the action close to the surface it affects.
Use extended mode when the icon is ambiguous.
dont: Do not put multiple actions inside FAB.
Do not cover critical content or controls.
Do not use FAB for global navigation.
info: Check target size and safe area.
Check overlap with maps, sheets, and bottom navigation.

agentInstructions: Use FAB for create, add movement, center map, scan receipt, or start route when it is the sole primary action.
Use extended FAB when the label prevents ambiguity.
Use loading only for the invoked action.
rejectIf: FAB contains more than one command.
The icon has no accessible label.
